historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_3yr_cagr (FY2023-FY2026, measured from the post-WFS-equity-raise base so the acquisition financing is not counted as growth)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.6% 3yr / 12.2% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue CAGR (53.4% / 45.6%). The revenue and FCF CAGRs are not growth rates: they span the COVID trough (FY2021-FY2023) and the WFS acquisition step-change (FY2024). EPS CAGRs are undefined (FY2021 and FY2023 EPS negative); FY2019-FY2026 EPS CAGR is -2.3% because the WFS deal was part equity-funded and is still deleveraging. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR undefined (FY2023 owner FCF negative).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF history here = reported pre-lease FCF - SBC (no equity-award taxes; interest income not stripped because SATS is net debt). The SBC-adjusted 5yr FCF CAGR (68.9%) is meaningless for the same reason as revenue. Forward drivers are anchored to FY2025-FY2026 actuals (revenue +13.0% then +9.0%; adj. EBITDA margin 18.6%) and to the FY2029 targets.

scenario_narratives.base: WFS integration keeps compounding but more slowly than the FY2025 rebound: cargo volumes keep outgrowing IATA's benchmark on hub-carrier wins (Riyadh Air, Azul, Cathay, Saudia Cargo) and new capacity (Heathrow 2027, Brussels, Madrid, Bengaluru), revenue grows 7% decelerating to 2.5%, and AI/automation lifts the pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 18.6% to 20%. Revenue reaches ~S$7.8bn in FY2029, slightly short of the >S$8bn ambition, with the growth-capex wave easing back to ~4% of revenue and cash taxes normalising upward as WFS jurisdictions catch up.
scenario_narratives.bull: SATS hits and beats its FY2029 plan: consolidation of airlines onto fewer integrated handlers drives contract wins across the 225-station network, e-commerce cargo (Amazon Express across 12 US gateways, EFFH in Europe) keeps cargo share gains going, revenue clears S$8bn by FY2029 and the margin pushes past 21% as hub automation and cross-sell scale. Deleveraging frees cash for rising dividends and bolt-on M&A.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle and geopolitics bite: Gulf hub disruption and US tariff changes keep Americas and Middle East cargo soft, US low-cost-carrier schedule cuts weigh on ground handling, and wage inflation across 27 countries meets aggressive rebidding by Swissport, dnata and Menzies, so the margin stalls at ~18% and revenue grows only 2-4%. Lease costs creep up as new facilities open ahead of volume, and working capital absorbs cash. FY2029 targets are missed and ROE stays near 10%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on the post-WFS business only, with leases treated as an operating cost (full lease cash deducted, lease liabilities out of net debt), associates/JVs and NCI handled in the equity bridge, and SBC expensed with a flat share count. The pre-FY2024 history is a different business and is used only for context.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lease treatment: switching to leases-as-debt without charging lease renewals would overstate value by roughly the S$1.76bn lease liability; the full lease cash is ~2.5x the SBC-adjusted FCF after leases, so the lease line is the most sensitive driver
Terminal multiple cap (14x base) binds below Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% (~20x), so terminal value depends on the cap, not on terminal growth
Air cargo and travel cyclicality and geopolitical trade-lane disruption (Gulf hubs, US tariffs)
Wage inflation against limited pricing power in a labour-intensive outsourced-services model
Associates/JVs at book (S$771m) may understate their value if SoAJV reaches the >S$150m target; NCI valued by multiple, not market

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.17-4.96
data_sources.financials: SATS Annual Report FY2026 (year ended 31 March 2026): income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement, notes 7, 10, 16, 20, 21, 28; Metrics.csv FY2015-FY2026 built from 47 filings
data_sources.qualitative: S58.SI_Analysis.json (FY2029 ambitions from the 2Q FY2026 results presentation and FY2026 Annual Report)

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares FY2026 (Annual Report FY2026 note 10: 1,513.6m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and SATS bought back S$56.5m of treasury shares in FY2026 (S$33.1m FY2025), so the flat count is being funded by actual repurchases. No non-SBC issuance modelled (the FY2023 WFS equity raise is history; leverage target already met).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash flow statement, 'Share-based compensation expense' add-back S$34.7m (FY2025 S$45.3m). No equity-award tax withholding line exists (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year).
inputs.fx_note: Verified, not assumed: the FY2026 statements are presented in Singapore dollars ($ million) and the SGX quote for S58.SI is SGD (Yahoo chart meta currency SGD). No FX bridge needed. WFS operations earn mostly USD/EUR, but they are translated into SGD in the statements, so the flows being discounted are SGD.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T09:04:18Z (SGX regular close, Friday 23 Oct 2026; not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: SGD-built WACC 7.5%, same in all three scenarios (risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not the rate). Cost of equity ~9.0% = SGD 10y SGS ~2.4% + beta ~1.1 x ERP ~5.5% + ~0.5% for cyclical aviation exposure. After-tax cost of debt ~4.0% (USD notes 4.83% coupon, term loans 1.2-8.3%; ~22% blended tax shield). Weights at market: equity ~S$5.4bn vs borrowings S$2.4bn (leases excluded under treatment B) -> ~70/30. 0.70 x 9.0 + 0.30 x 4.0 = 7.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full lease cash payment (FY2026 'Payment of lease liabilities' S$469.7m in financing = principal plus S$122.3m lease interest, 'Repayment of leases and related charges' per note 28) is deducted via lease_cost_pct_path (7.4% of revenue; FY2025 7.6%). Lease liabilities (S$1,760.9m = 1,454.2 non-current + 306.7 current) are EXCLUDED from net debt, so total_debt here (S$2,375.2m notes and borrowings, note 28) is lower than core_metrics TotalDebt (S$4,136.1m, which includes leases). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2026 D&A 603.1 - ROU depreciation 385.0 = 218.1, 3.4% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of subsidiaries); NCI charged once, in the equity bridge, at ~12x FY2026 NCI profit share of S$19.9m = S$240m (book NCI S$186.4m).
inputs.associates_treatment: Consolidated EBITDA excludes share of results of associates/JVs (S$114.5m FY2026 net of tax; dividends received S$64.7m). That income stream is not in the flows, so its source asset is added in the bridge at book: investment in associates S$463.4m + joint ventures S$307.5m = S$770.9m (~6.7x the after-tax share of results, i.e. conservative; management targets SoAJV >S$150m by FY2029).
inputs.interest_treatment: Component build is unlevered (adj. EBITDA -> tax on EBIT -> capex), so the S$129.5m interest paid to third parties that sits inside reported OCF is not in the projected flows; borrowings are deducted once in net debt. Finance income (S$12.2m) is likewise outside EBITDA and the cash sits in the bridge, so no interest-income strip is needed (the company is net debt, not net cash).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (SGD WACC, lease treatment B, NCI and associates in the bridge). Routing: SATS is an operating company (airport ground handling, air-cargo terminals via WFS, aviation and non-aviation food solutions), not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco -> SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF). Structural break: the WFS acquisition (completed April 2023, FY2024) roughly tripled revenue (FY2023 S$1.76bn -> FY2024 S$5.15bn) and added S$2bn+ of borrowings plus lease liabilities; pre-FY2024 history is a different, smaller, net-cash Singapore-centric business plus a COVID trough (FY2021-FY2023), so FY2026 is the base year and growth/margin paths are anchored to FY2025-FY2026 and the FY2029 targets, not to historical CAGRs. Base-year reconciliation: FY2026 owner FCF after leases = SATS-defined FCF after lease payments S$215.8m - SBC 34.7 = S$181.1m, which is also after S$129.5m interest paid; unlevered equivalent ~S$280m. Pre-lease FCF (OCF - capex, the Metrics.csv FreeCashFlow column) is S$685.5m. FY2026 capex (S$344.7m, 5.4% of revenue) is elevated by growth projects (Changi S$250m 5-year commitment, Heathrow cargo facility opening 2027, Brussels/Madrid/Bengaluru); the paths glide it back toward ~4%. FY2029 targets cross-check (revenue >S$8bn, EBITDA margin >20%, EBIT >10%): base reaches ~S$7.8bn revenue and ~19.4% reported EBITDA margin in FY2029 (slightly short of target); bull reaches ~S$8.3bn and ~20.4% (target met); bear ~S$7.0bn and ~17.9%. Price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.17-4.96.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Adj. EBITDA is pre-SBC: FY2026 reported 18.1% + SBC 0.55% = 18.6%. Base reaches ~19.4% reported (20.0% pre-SBC) in FY2029, a touch under the >20% target, then holds.
base.capex_note: FY2026 5.4% is a growth-capex peak; FY2024-FY2025 3.6-3.8%. Glides to 4.0% terminal, above D&A ex-ROU (3.5%) to fund ~2.5% perpetual growth.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Unlevered cash tax on EBIT after leases. FY2026 cash tax paid S$82.8m plus ~S$25m interest shield on ~S$458m EBIT ~ 23-24%; book tax S$111.1m implies higher; cash tax paid nearly doubled FY2025->FY2026 as WFS jurisdictions (US 21%+state, Europe 25%+) catch up. Ramps to 26%.
base.wc_note: Services business; FY2026 working capital was a S$24.7m inflow on S$524m revenue growth (payables-funded). Held at zero rather than credited.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): the business is cyclical air-traffic and trade exposure with live geopolitical disruption, labour-intensive with limited pricing power, and still carries S$2.4bn of borrowings plus S$1.8bn of leases. Base 50%: FY2026 delivered +9% revenue and margin expansion on plan, consistent with a slightly-short-of-target path. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): the bull case needs several independent things at once (volume share gains, >21% margin, contained wage inflation), and SoAJV is already lagging its FY2029 target.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
